Launch CodingManageR Locally (Single-User SQLite Mode)

Source: R/app.R
run_app_local.Rd

Constructs and returns a shiny.appobj strictly configured for local, single-user workstation use with a local SQLite database file. Any MYSQL_HOST or MYSQL_USER environment variables present on the machine are ignored so local sessions never connect accidentally to a remote server.

Usage

run_app_local(sqlite_path = NULL, empty = TRUE)

Arguments

sqlite_path

Optional file path to a local SQLite database. Passing a different .sqlite path creates or reopens a separate, isolated project; the parent directory must already exist.

empty

Logical passed to seed_initial_data() when initializing a fresh database. Defaults to TRUE (creates only the default admin and historic_user accounts). When FALSE, demonstration data is only inserted into a brand-new, empty database; existing SQLite files or databases that already contain rows are left untouched and trigger a warning.

Value

A shiny.appobj object that launches the local Shiny portal when printed or run interactively.

Details

To manage multiple independent local projects on one computer, supply a distinct sqlite_path file for each study (each .sqlite file stores its own scales, sources, case texts, user accounts, ratings, and training logs). Re-passing the same sqlite_path reopens that project. When sqlite_path is NULL (and no SQLITE_PATH environment variable is set), a single default database is stored under tools::R_user_dir("CodingManageR", which = "data"). Always stop the running Shiny app before copying, renaming, moving, or archiving a .sqlite file so SQLite merges its Write-Ahead Log (-wal/-shm) cleanly.

For multi-user server deployments backed by MySQL/MariaDB, use run_app_server() instead.

See also

run_app_server(), run_app()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Launch the default local SQLite project
run_app_local()

# Launch separate local projects in isolated SQLite files
run_app_local(sqlite_path = "study_a.sqlite")
run_app_local(sqlite_path = "study_b.sqlite")

# Launch a temporary demo session with sample data
run_app_local(sqlite_path = tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"), empty = FALSE)
} # }
